items.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: the people coming in were supposed to be Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie, after us.

ctx.x: You said something about bebop. My introduction to that was eye-opening as well as astounding. We had just finished, after the Army we had a little group called The Swing Wing which came out of the Santa Ana group led by Milt DeLugg, an accordion player, I gravitate to accordions somehow, he was like a commercial cat. And we were partners, 70/30. We were partners 70/30, right? Because I was a soloist and he was — so we

played this thing and the people coming in were supposed to be Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie, after us. And I wasn’t listening to the bebop stuff, I mean Charlie Parker then. And this fellow comes up to me the last night before closing night, he came up and said, “I dig your playing.” And so I said, “Thank you very much,” and I usually enjoy it when people come up and say I like your playing. I went in the next night and there was Charlie Parker, who had said, “I dig your playing, man.” So that was my…
